title: A picture added to a PDF page looks blurry and pixelated at zoom
trigger: Owner's iPad, screenshot of Q2.pdf: insert a picture on a page, view it at reading zoom
cause: Sharpness is lost when the picture is added, not when it is drawn. PDFSession.addPicture (Sources/GraphiteUI/PDFSessionPictures.swift:52) prepares it for 60% of the page width, and DrawingPictures.picture keeps only 2 pixels per point of that width (DrawingPictures.swift:35, preferredPNGScale 2 at Sources/GraphiteCore/DrawingPayload.swift:149), JPEG 0.9. A 12 MP photo on A4 becomes 715 px wide; the original is not kept. That is 1.36x enlarged at fit-width in iPad portrait, 3x at zoom 3, and worse once the picture is dragged larger (movePicture only changes bounds). The owner's Q2.pdf screenshot shows a picture about 80% of the page wide, which fits a picture enlarged past the prepared 60%. A paste with a known width gets 4 px/pt, still far below the zoomed screen.
evidence: findings/shots/owner-blurry-picture-pdf.webp
fix: Keep the picture's full resolution and redraw at zoom
verdict_reason: Owner's device report; the cause follows from DrawingPictures.swift:35 and PDFSessionPictures.swift:52, and drawing is not at fault (PDFPicture.swift:215 uses high interpolation from those stored pixels).
evidence_level: owner's device

title: A highlighter stroke turns into a solid band that hides the text under it once saved: in Graphite after a relaunch, on the Mac, in Preview and in other apps
trigger: On iPad, highlight a line of PDF text with the bar's highlighter (default #f6d743, opacity 1). Open the PDF on the Mac or in Preview.
cause: PencilStrokeSampler.color gives alpha = ink alpha * min(average point opacity, 1). A marker's point opacity is 1.5 (EvenHighlighter.tipOpacity), so the result is the ink's alpha, 1 for the bar's preset. PDFOutlinedInkAnnotation fills the outline with that colour in normal blend mode; no multiply is set anywhere in the ink path, unlike text markup, whose PDFMarkupColor relies on readers' multiply. PencilKit itself draws a marker translucently (about 0.8 to 0.9 and under dark ink), so on the iPad's canvas the text is readable, which hides the problem until the file is opened elsewhere. The same opaque band shows on the iPad wherever annotations show: thumbnails and a page whose stored ink is still decoding. Exports replay the same annotations.
evidence: alpha: Double(components.alpha * min(max(averageOpacity, 0), 1))
fix: For marker ink, write a multiply blend mode in the appearance (setBlendMode(.multiply) in the outline's draw) or a translucent alpha.
verdict_reason: PencilStrokeSampler.swift:37-41 clamps point opacity to 1; EvenHighlighter.swift records that PencilKit gives marker points 1.3 to 1.5, so a real marker's alpha equals the tool's, 1 by default (PencilToolbox.swift:99, 504). PDFInkAnnotation.swift:46-100 fills with normal blending and no multiply exists in the ink path, so the band covers the text in saved files. Not limited to the even-highlighter option.
evidence_level: seen on iPad simulator
seen_note: Highlight strokes are see-through when drawn and turn into solid yellow that hides the text after a relaunch, so this also happens inside Graphite.

title: Ink looks blurry once it settles in Graphite
trigger: Owner's iPad: draw on a PDF page and look at the stroke after pen-up or after reopening
cause: Traced: while a canvas covers a page the annotations are hidden (GraphitePDFView.swift:1366 and setInkAnnotationsHidden), so settled ink is PencilKit's bitmap tiles, drawn at the canvas scale and shrunk or enlarged to the zoom by layer transforms. renderingScale(forZoom:) rounds zoom up to 0.5 steps (line 676), so pixels map one to one only at exact multiples of 0.5 (zoom 1.36 uses scale 1.5, shown at 0.91). The scale is also capped at 3 and lowered by a broad tool (lines 662, 668, 684), which magnifies all ink on the page. The saved vector outlines are not the source.
evidence: owner report
fix: Render settled ink as vectors at the current zoom
verdict_reason: Owner's device report. The code path is read (GraphitePDFView.swift:662-689, 740-752, 1366); that resampling is the visible loss, and not something else inside PencilKit, is the best trace but is not provable by reading.
device_check: On the iPad, write at zoom 1.36 and at exactly 1.5 and compare screenshots of the same stroke; if 1.5 is crisp and 1.36 soft the rounding is the cause, if both are soft look inside PencilKit's tiles.
evidence_level: owner's device

title: Ink drawn while zoomed in lands about 2.7 times too thick on the page, and stays thick after zooming back out and after relaunch
trigger: PDF in portrait, pen, finger drawing on. A stroke at fit zoom measures 4.58 px; pinch to about 3.27x and the old stroke scales to 15.04 px, correct; a new stroke there measures 39.7 px. Back at 0.91x: old stroke 4.15 px, the stroke drawn while zoomed 11.07 px, a fresh stroke 4.23 px. Widths are unchanged after relaunch. Simulator, iOS 27.0, 2x screenshot.
cause: PDFPageCanvasView.toolForDrawing multiplies the tool width by the canvas zoomScale, on the assumption written in its comment that PencilKit keeps a tool as wide on screen at any canvas zoom. The measurement shows the width is applied again, so it lands up to the rendering scale (cap 3) too thick. InkWidthAtZoomTests only checks tool.width / zoomScale and never measures a stroke, so it passes. Docs/Goodnotes-writing-feel.md already says this assumption needs confirming on the iPad.
evidence: owner report
fix: Stop scaling the tool, or scale by what a measurement of PKStroke point sizes shows; add a test that measures a saved stroke at zoom 1 and 3; check once with a real Pencil on the iPad.
verdict_reason: Owner's device report, so the symptom stands. What the code proves is only that width on the page is meant to be constant (GraphitePDFView.swift:624, App/Tests/InkWidthAtZoomTests.swift); the cause of the excess is PencilKit's stroke width at a zoomed canvas, and part of what the owner sees may be the deliberate wider-on-screen behaviour.
device_check: Write the same word at PDF zoom 1, 2 and 3 with pen 2.8 and monoline, log each stroke's stored point size, and measure the exported widths. Also ask the owner whether the complaint is width on the page after zooming back, or width on screen while zoomed: the second is the design and is what Goodnotes does.
evidence_level: seen on iPad simulator

title: Undo stops working on a PDF page after lasso or highlighter use: it says "The ink on this page changed in a way this step does not know" and the stroke stays
trigger: Lasso ink, hold and drag the frame with one hand, tap Undo in the palette or press Command-Z with the other.
cause: During a drag the canvas shows the drawing without the selected strokes through showWithoutRecording. change.reverting(canvas.drawing) then sees another stroke count and returns nil, so applyInkFromHistory throws inkChangedOutsideHistory. registerStep's catch only sets errorMessage, and the step is not registered again, so it has left the history for good.
evidence: guard let drawing = transform(canvas.drawing) else { throw Self.inkChangedOutsideHistory }
fix: Disable undo during a selection drag, or cancel the drag before applying.
verdict_reason: InkSelection.swift:594 shows the drawing without the selected strokes during a drag; PencilDrawingChange.swift:98 returns nil on another stroke count, PDFEditHistory.swift:303 throws, and :98-103 only records the error, so the step is gone. No undo guard during a drag was found (UndoAvailability.swift:54, dragStart is used only in InkSelection). Rare: needs a second hand during a drag.
evidence_level: seen on iPad simulator
seen_note: After lasso and highlighter use, Undo said the ink changed in a way the step does not know, three times running; a relaunch cleared it.

title: Resizing handwriting with the lasso changes its weight far more than its size: shrunk by half it nearly vanishes, shrunk further it disappears
trigger: Lasso a written word in pen and drag the corner to half its size.
cause: InkSelectionController.stroke multiplies each point's size by the scale. The repo's own measurement (PencilInkRenderedWidth) is that pen, monoline and fountain pen draw 2*size-4, nothing below size 2. So the drawn width is not proportional. Pen at size 4.8 draws 5.6. At 0.5x: size 2.4 draws 0.8 where 2.8 is expected, 3.5x too thin. At 0.4x: size 1.92 draws nothing, and the stroke is gone from the canvas and from the annotation. At 2x: size 9.6 draws 15.2 where 11.2 is expected, 36% too heavy. Goodnotes scales ink exactly with the word (x0.455 for x0.456, Docs/Goodnotes-writing-feel.md).
evidence: size: CGSize(width: point.size.width * sizeScale, height: point.size.height * sizeScale)
fix: Scale the drawn width: newSize = pointSize(forRenderedWidth: renderedWidth(size) * scale), per ink, using PencilInkRenderedWidth.
verdict_reason: InkSelection.swift:700-706 does multiply point size by the scale, with only a frame-size minimum (:531), and PencilInkRenderedWidth.swift records 2*size-4 with nothing below size 2. The result rests on that table holding for these rebuilt points, which only rendering can show; no test measures a resized stroke's drawn width.
device_check: Lasso a pen word, shrink to 0.5x and 0.4x, and check whether strokes thin out of proportion or vanish; undo restores them.
evidence_level: path traced, needs a device check

title: Lasso over a stroke drawn while zoomed in selects nothing, only an empty area with just 'Take Screenshot'; a normal stroke in the same loop selects with Cut/Copy/Duplicate
trigger: Same PDF page: stroke A drawn at fit zoom, stroke B drawn at about 3.3x zoom (see zoomed-ink finding), zoomed back to fit. Lasso tool in the fixed bar, loop clearly around B only (three loops tried, B fully inside): result is the dashed area with a menu holding only 'Take Screenshot', ink not selected. Loop around A: selected, menu Cut, Copy, Duplicate, Take Screenshot. Evidence live-ipad-3.png (B, no selection) and live-ipad-4.png (A selected).
cause: Not traced. Stroke B's geometry or stored coordinate space differs from a stroke drawn at zoom 1 (same root as the 2.7x width), so the lasso hit test does not see it; the menu falls back to areaMenuElements when no stroke is selected.
evidence: InkSelection.swift: if (configuration.identifier as? String) == MenuIdentifier.area { return UIMenu(children: areaMenuElements()) }
fix: Check how the zoomed canvas's stroke path points are stored vs the lasso's page-space loop and select by the same space.
evidence_level: seen on iPad simulator

title: Choosing a broad pencil or highlighter makes all the ink on the page blurry when zoomed in, and past zoom 3 all ink is blurry anyway
trigger: Zoom a page to 3. Choose a pencil at 16 pt or a highlighter at 28 pt, or just zoom past 3.
cause: renderingScale = min(zoom step, tool limit, 3). largestRenderingScale(keepingWidthOf:) gives pencil 7 pt -> 2, pencil 16 pt -> 1, highlighter 28 pt -> 2, pen 12 pt -> 2. The limit comes from the tool in hand but applies to the whole canvas and to every page's canvas, in Read mode as well, since configure takes the tool regardless of input.isEnabled. So at zoom 3 with a 16 pt pencil chosen, all earlier fine pen ink is drawn at s=1 and magnified 3x; with pencil 7 pt, 1.5x. Past the cap of 3, ink is magnified zoom/3: 1.33x at zoom 4. PDFView's maxScaleFactor is never set, so PDFKit allows zooming past the cap. Switching between such a tool and a pen at high zoom also re-tiles every kept canvas at each switch, so the page visibly changes sharpness with the tool. Docs/Architecture.md records this as a trade-off ('a broad pencil or highlighter zoomed in draws its ink less sharp').
evidence: var renderingScale: CGFloat { min(zoomRenderingScale, toolRenderingScaleLimit) }
fix: Do not tie canvas resolution to the tool: normalise the new stroke's width at pen-up, or give broad tools a separate unscaled path, and limit PDF zoom or raise the cap on visible pages.
verdict_reason: GraphitePDFView.swift:662 takes the minimum of zoom and tool limit for the whole canvas, :684-689 gives pencil 16 pt scale 1 and pencil 7 pt scale 2, :668 caps at 3 and maxScaleFactor is never set (the test itself uses zoom 3.2). Documented as a trade-off in Docs/Architecture.md line 218, kept because the owner reports blurry settled ink. Lowered: the owner's bar presets (pen 2.8, pencil 2.4, highlighter 18) hit only the past-zoom-3 part.
evidence_level: traced in code by two readers

title: Ink changes weight when the saved version shows instead of the live one: a moment after a page appears, on the Mac, and in other apps
trigger: Scroll a Read-mode PDF to a densely inked page whose canvas was released. Then compare iPad with the same PDF on the Mac.
cause: While the stored drawing decodes, the canvas is hidden and the page's annotations show. The live document's are plain ink: one average width and flat colour (PDFInkAnnotationFactory with drawsOutline false). When the decode ends the canvas replaces them, so ink jumps in weight and texture. Saved outlines are not the same either: Docs/Architecture.md measures them 16 to 29% heavier than PencilKit's ink. Highlighter and fountain pen are saved at the point size (renderedWidth returns nil), though the marker draws about 1.35x its size (markerMeasurements: size 24 draws 32.5) and the fountain pen 2*size-4. A page written on iPad therefore differs in weight on the Mac. Reload on iPad stays the same, because the same PKDrawing comes back.
evidence: canvas.isHidden = !input.isEnabled && canvas.isRestoringStoredInk
fix: Use the outline in the live document too, and add width tables for marker and fountain pen.
verdict_reason: GraphitePDFView.swift:1366-1370 shows plain annotations while the stored drawing decodes and the canvas after, and the comment at :1351-1356 says those lines have one width and flat color. PencilStrokeSampler.swift:104-109 saves marker and fountain pen at point size. The hunter's 16 to 29% predates the 2026-10-20 width fix for pen and monoline (Goodnotes-writing-feel.md table), so on the Mac the excess now concerns marker, fountain pen and slightly pencil, not all ink.
evidence_level: traced in code by two readers

title: Making a placed picture bigger makes it blurrier still, though the code says it stays sharp
trigger: Add a photo, drag its corner until it fills the page width.
cause: addPicture prepares pixels for 60% of the page width and the comment claims 'Prepared at the widest it is placed, so it stays sharp when made larger later'. movePicture only changes bounds and never goes back to the source, which is gone. A4 at full width: 715 px over 595 pt = 1.2 px/pt, so 2.27x enlarged at fit-width in portrait and 5x at zoom 3. The drawing editor prepares for the full canvas width (760 pt * 2 = 1520 px); the PDF path does not.
evidence: let preparedWidth = shownPictureWidth * (preferredWidth == nil ? 1 : Self.pastedPictureSharpnessFactor)
fix: Prepare for the whole page width at least, whatever size it is first shown at.
verdict_reason: PDFSessionPictures.swift:52 prepares for 60% of the page, the comment at line 59 claims it stays sharp when made larger, and movePicture (line 80 onward) only changes bounds with no source to return to. Same root as the owner's blurry picture but a separate trigger and a separate wrong claim in the code.
evidence_level: traced in code by two readers

title: Dots written with one touch, like the dot of an i or a full stop, are missing from the saved PDF and from SVG or PDF drawings
trigger: Write a one-point dot on a PDF page, save, open the PDF on the Mac or in Preview. Or export a drawing with such a dot as SVG or PDF.
cause: centerLineSamples uses path.interpolatedPoints(by: .distance(1)). InkSelection.swift documents and handles the fact that a dot with a single control point interpolates to nothing ('A dot has no interpolated points'). The sampler has no such fallback, so visibleSegments is empty and portableStroke returns nil at 'guard !widths.isEmpty', which treats it as erased: name '', no annotation. The PKDrawing record still holds it, so the iPad's canvas shows it and the bug stays hidden there. PencilVectorConverter drops it the same way. PDFInkAnnotationFactory's 'A single tap still needs a visible mark' branch is never reached with empty samples. How often a real Pencil tap has exactly one control point was not measured here.
evidence: guard !widths.isEmpty else { return nil }
fix: Fall back to the control points as InkSelection.samplePoints does, and use the point's size for width.
verdict_reason: PencilStrokeSampler.swift:104-110 has no fallback and PDFPencilInk.swift:214-215 returns nil on no samples, and InkSelection.swift:438 states a dot has no interpolated points. Whether a real Pencil tap yields a stroke like that is PencilKit's behaviour and unmeasured (the hunter says so), hence lowered from high.
device_check: Tap dots with the Pencil on a PDF page, log control point counts and interpolated counts, and open the saved file in Preview.
evidence_level: path traced, needs a device check

title: In the drawing editor the same pen width lands thicker on a phone or narrow window and thinner when zoomed in
trigger: Open a 760 pt drawing on an iPhone (zoom 390/760 = 0.51) with a 2.4 pt pencil or a 10 pt highlighter. Or on iPad zoom 4x with a 7 pt pencil.
cause: InfiniteCanvasView.toolForDrawing multiplies the width by zoom with no limit, and PencilKit holds each ink to validWidthRange (PencilInk.widthRange mirrors it). Zoom 0.51: pencil 2.4 -> 1.23, raised to 2.4, lands 4.68 in the drawing, nearly 2x; highlighter 10 -> 5.1, raised to 7.5, lands 14.6, +46%; pen 1.6 -> 0.82, raised to 0.9, lands 1.75. Zoom 4.3 (iPad fit 1.08 * 4): pencil 7 -> 30, held to 16, lands 3.7, about half; highlighter 18 -> 77, held to 60, lands 14. The PDF path has a limit for the upper bound and never goes below 1; this path has neither. Docs/Architecture.md mentions only the upper case. The lower clamp is inferred from widthRange and validated presets, not measured.
evidence: Self.tool(super.toolForDrawing(chosenTool), scaledBy: zoomScale)
fix: Normalise stroke point sizes at pen-up to the chosen width in the drawing instead of relying on the tool's clamped width.
verdict_reason: DrawingEditor.swift:1080-1082 scales with no limit, unlike the PDF canvas's limit. The upper clamp is measured (Goodnotes-writing-feel.md table, pencil 16); the lower one, which is the iPhone half of the title, is inferred from PencilInk.widthRange (PencilToolbox.swift:54-65) and has not been measured on a scaled tool.
device_check: On iPhone at drawing zoom 0.51 read canvas.tool width for a pencil 2.4 and measure the exported stroke; on iPad at 4x do the same with pencil 7.
evidence_level: path traced, needs a device check

title: A stroke started right after a pinch can have its canvas resized under it mid-stroke
trigger: Pinch to another zoom step, then start writing within 0.2 s and keep writing.
cause: scheduleRenderingScaleUpdate fires 0.2 s after the last scale change and updateRenderingScale never checks whether a stroke is under way. setRenderingScale leads to layoutSubviews, which changes canvas.bounds, zoomScale, contentOffset and transform, then calls retakeChosenTool, which replaces canvas.tool, all during PencilKit's active drawing gesture. The same happens when a pinch by the other hand ends mid-stroke. The stroke's live points were at the old canvas scale. What PencilKit then does with it was not measured.
evidence: for canvas in canvasesByPage.values { canvas.overlayView?.setRenderingScale(scale) }
fix: Defer the scale change until drawingGestureRecognizer is back to .possible.
verdict_reason: GraphitePDFView.swift:908-921 has no check for a stroke under way and layoutSubviews :740-752 changes bounds, zoom, transform and tool. The hunter admits the visible result is unmeasured, and it depends on what PencilKit does with an active stroke.
device_check: Pinch across a 0.5 step and start writing within 0.2 s; look for a jump, a width change or a lost stroke.
evidence_level: path traced, needs a device check

title: Zooming in on an inked PDF can use hundreds of MB, and nothing is released on a memory warning, so the app can be killed while writing
trigger: Open a dense A3 notebook, zoom to 3, scroll through several pages, then keep writing.
cause: Up to 6 hidden canvases plus the displayed ones are kept (retainedHiddenCanvasCount) and every kept canvas's overlay takes the new scale. Docs/Architecture.md: 'PencilKit keeps tiles for the whole canvas, on screen or not'. On a 2x screen at s=3 an A4 canvas is 3572x5052 px, 72 MB if fully tiled, about 580 MB for 8 canvases; A3 is 144 MB each, over 1 GB. GraphitePDFView registers no didReceiveMemoryWarning (only the Markdown editor and tab thumbnails do), so hidden canvases are not dropped under pressure. Being killed loses strokes from the last 2 s, since autosave runs 2 s after the last edit. Actual allocation per canvas depends on PencilKit and was not measured.
evidence: private static let retainedHiddenCanvasCount = 6
fix: Keep hidden canvases at scale 1, and release them on a memory warning after recording their ink.
verdict_reason: retainedHiddenCanvasCount 6 (GraphitePDFView.swift:775), scale applied to kept canvases (:920), and no memory warning handler in this file (only NativeMarkdownEditor, MarkdownEditorRetention, TabThumbnails). The MB figures assume full tiling of hidden canvases, taken from a code comment at :666, and a kept canvas whose overlay PDFKit released takes no new scale (:920 uses overlayView?). Needs a memory measurement.
device_check: Instruments Allocations on a dense A3 notebook at zoom 3 while scrolling 8 pages.
evidence_level: path traced, needs a device check

title: Scrolling a densely written PDF stutters, even just reading, because each new page is read several times on the main thread
trigger: Scroll through a notebook whose pages have thousands of strokes (the owner's sheet has 6,143 on a page) in Read mode.
cause: pdfView(_:overlayViewFor:) makes a PKCanvasView for every page shown, Read mode included, and configure() always calls restoreStoredInkIfNeeded, though the comment on hasRestoredStoredInk says pages only viewed never pay. On the main actor each page then has: PDFInkGroups.newGroup (scan of all annotations), editableGroup (scan, value(forAnnotationKey:) and persistentName for every annotation, base64 decode of the whole record, decoding and comparing all names), setInkAnnotationsHidden (scan), and when the background decode ends editableGroup again in full, then configure's scan again. Only PKDrawing(data:) is off the main thread. Pages past the 6 retained canvases repeat all of it when scrolled back. Time per scan on the device was not measured here.
evidence: guard let editableGroup = PDFInkGroups.editableGroup(on: page) else { ... }
fix: Read the record once off the main path, compare a version number rather than decoding twice, and create canvases only when writing or when the page has ink.
verdict_reason: pdfView(_:overlayViewFor:) (:1238) makes a canvas for every shown page and configure (:1357 onward) always restores, contrary to the comment at :589-591; PDFInkAnnotation.swift:269-295 scans and base64-decodes on the main actor, and repeats after the decode (:1329). The cost per page is unmeasured, so stutter is not proven.
device_check: Time Profiler while scrolling the 6,143-stroke sheet in Read mode.
evidence_level: path traced, needs a device check

title: Annotating a PDF embedded in a note: a resting hand scrolls the note under the Pencil
trigger: Tap Annotate on an embedded PDF in a note and write with the hand resting on the page.
cause: configureEnclosingScrollViews only removes the Pencil from the note scroll view's pan, and raises minimum touches when drawing with a finger. makeWaitForPalmRejection is applied only to scrollViews(in: view), the PDF's own, never to enclosing ones. With the default Pencil-only input one finger still pans the note. The hand's touch is taken by palm rejection, which stops the PDF's scroll from moving, and the note's pan has nothing telling it to wait.
evidence: scrollView.panGestureRecognizer.allowedTouchTypes = restriction.panTouchTypes.filter { touchType in touchType != pencil }
fix: Make the enclosing scroll views' pan wait for palm rejection too while annotating, removing the wait when annotating ends.
verdict_reason: GraphitePDFView.swift:1119 applies the wait only to the PDF's own scroll views and :1191-1192 leave one-finger pan on the note. Whether a resting hand then moves the note depends on what iPadOS rejects itself and how the nested pans resolve.
device_check: Annotate an embedded PDF in a long note with the hand resting and moving slightly; watch whether the note scrolls.
evidence_level: path traced, needs a device check

title: Pausing while writing on a full page may cause a hitch at each autosave
trigger: Write on a page with thousands of strokes, pause 2 s, go on writing.
cause: Autosave runs 2 s after the last stroke. save() calls writePendingInkRecords on the main actor. For every kept canvas (up to 8) writeDeferredInkRecords runs recordUnrecordedInk, which fingerprints every stroke of both drawings via PencilDrawingChange(from:to:), and writeDeferredInkRecord, which archives the whole drawing with dataRepresentation. The pen-up work was made cheap (2.1 ms measured), but this moved the page-sized cost here. A stroke begun at that moment waits. Then the background save rewrites the file; BUG-IMPORT-03 measures minutes for pages with thousands of strokes, and autosaveDelay caps at 30 s, so a slow file is rewritten nearly all the time. Main-thread time for the save step was not measured here.
evidence: for canvas in canvasesByPage.values { recordUnrecordedInk(of: canvas); writeDeferredInkRecord(of: canvas) }
fix: Skip canvases whose drawing did not change since the last record with a dirty flag, and archive off the main thread from an immutable PKDrawing copy.
verdict_reason: Overstated: writeDeferredInkRecord archives only canvases with a deferred record (GraphitePDFView.swift:1552), so the archive is not done for all 8 canvases and the suggested dirty flag exists. What remains is recordUnrecordedInk fingerprinting every stroke of every kept canvas on the main actor (:1461-1476, PencilDrawingChange.swift:32-33) plus one archive for the edited page, at each save (PDFSession.swift:491). Time unmeasured.
device_check: Time writeDeferredInkRecords on the main thread with a 6,143-stroke page and several kept canvases.
evidence_level: path traced, needs a device check

title: Each Rotate Right or Crop on a placed picture lowers its quality again
trigger: Tap Rotate Right four times on a placed JPEG picture, back to where it started.
cause: rotatedClockwise and cropped decode and re-encode the JPEG at quality 0.92 each time, on top of the 0.9 at placement. Four turns are five JPEG generations of a picture that looks unchanged. Undo restores the older bytes, repeating a rotate does not.
evidence: static let photographQuality = 0.92
fix: Keep the prepared bytes and store the quarter turns, or re-encode losslessly.
verdict_reason: PDFSessionPictures.swift rotatePictureRight and cropPicture go through PictureEditing.swift:17 and :33, and encode(like:) at :76-85 re-encodes a JPEG at 0.92 each time; the angle handle (rotatePicture) keeps the bytes and is unaffected. Low: a few generations at 0.92 are a slight loss.
evidence_level: traced in code by two readers

title: The shape preview while holding the Pencil is drawn up to 3 times too thick on a zoomed page, then snaps thinner at the lift
trigger: PDF at zoom 3, pen 2.8. Draw a line or circle with a pen not yet used at this zoom step and hold the Pencil at its end for 0.45 s.
cause: strokeTouchDidRest passes inkingTool.width as the preview width when no footprint exists. tool is the canvas's scaled tool (2.8*3 = 8.4 canvas points) and showShapePreview multiplies by zoomScale again: lineWidth = 8.4*3 = 25.2 canvas points = 8.4 pt on the page, 3 times the stroke (s times in general). footprintKey uses the scaled width, so every new zoom step has no footprint and hits this path again. With a footprint the preview is the raw point size times zoom, not the drawn width (pen size 4.8 draws 5.6).
evidence: width: Self.footprint(of: inkingTool)?.size.width ?? inkingTool.width ... shapePreviewLayer.lineWidth = max(width * zoomScale, 1)
fix: Convert to the drawing's width first (tool width / zoomScale) and key footprints by the width in the drawing, then apply the rendered-width table.
known: BUG-INK-02 is the same preview's geometry, not its width
verdict_reason: HistoryCanvasView.swift:584 falls back to inkingTool.width, which is already scaled (App/Tests/InkWidthAtZoomTests.swift reads canvas.tool width as chosen*zoom), and line 679 multiplies by zoomScale again: 3x on the page at scale 3. Hold-to-shape is on by default (StrokeHold.swift:41). Lowered to low: a preview lasting until the lift, only for the first hold at a new zoom step, since footprintKey includes the scaled width.
evidence_level: traced in code by two readers

title: A zoomed-in shape can come out as thick as a different pen, because shape widths are remembered by zoomed width
trigger: Draw with a 3 pt pen at canvas scale 2 (key 6.0). Pick a 2 pt pen, zoom so the canvas scale is 3 (key 6.0), hold a stroke into a shape and drag on.
cause: footprintsByTool is a static dictionary keyed by inkType and the canvas tool's scaled width. A 3 pt pen at scale 2 and a 2 pt pen at scale 3 share a key, so the dragged shape is built from the 3 pt stroke's point size, in drawing coordinates, and lands 50% thicker. The same pen at another zoom step has no entry, so the drag falls back to the plain stroke with no shape.
evidence: footprintsByTool[footprintKey(inkType: inkingTool.inkType, width: inkingTool.width)] = footprint
fix: Key the footprint by the chosen width in the drawing, tool.width / zoomScale.
verdict_reason: HistoryCanvasView.swift:515-526 keys footprints by scaled width and line 628 builds the dragged shape from that footprint, so collisions land at the wrong width; the bar's own pen sizes collide (1.6 at scale 3 and 4.8 at scale 1 both key 4.8, giving 3x). Only needs hold then drag at a coincidental zoom, hence low. HistoryCanvasView is UIKit, so iOS, not all.
evidence_level: traced in code by two readers
